title: Gatling and Locust: alternatives in Scala and in Python

videos.script: Lesson 5 wrote a load test in JavaScript. This lesson writes the same test twice more, in Java and in Python. {{same}} Gatling first. It was written in Scala, and its tests were Scala too. Today it speaks Java, Kotlin, Scala and JavaScript. {{gatling}} A Gatling user arrives, does the journey once, and leaves. You set how many arrive each second. {{arrive}} Its assertions hold lesson 1's requirement. When one is crossed, the Maven build fails, like a broken unit test. {{build}} Then Locust. Here the test is plain Python, and Locust is a library it imports. {{locust}} A Locust user stays for the whole test. It runs a task, waits, and picks the next one by weight. {{tasks}} Locust has no thresholds. So the locustfile judges the run itself, and sets the exit code. {{judge}} Last, how to choose. Not by which tool is fastest. By who on the team can read the test, and change it. {{choose}}
